indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B2.1.1.2: Understand the differences between living, non-living things and things which have never been alive
indicator.objective: Describe the basic structure of animals (head, limbs and trunk)

skills.description: Name the three basic parts of an animal
Identify the head, limbs, and trunk on a picture or real animal
State simply what each part does
Draw an animal and label the head, limbs, and trunk

misconceptions: Animals only have a head and legs; the trunk is not a part.
Limbs are only legs; arms/wings/fins are not limbs.
The trunk is the same as the tail.
All animals have the same number of limbs.

questions.stem: What are the three main parts of an animal's body?
hints: One is the head, one is the middle.
questions.explanation: The three basic parts of an animal are the head, limbs, and trunk.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse plant parts with animal parts.

questions.stem: What do we call the main body of an animal, where the head and limbs attach?
hints: It is not the head or the legs.
questions.explanation: The trunk is the main body of the animal.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the trunk is an elephant's nose.

questions.stem: What do we call the parts of an animal used for moving, like legs or arms?
hints: Birds have wings which are also these.
questions.explanation: Limbs are the parts used for movement (legs, arms, wings, fins).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think limbs are only legs.

questions.stem: Which part of an animal contains the eyes, ears, and mouth?
questions.explanation: The head contains the eyes, ears, and mouth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the head with the trunk.

questions.stem: What do animals use their limbs for?
questions.explanation: Animals use their limbs to move from place to place.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think limbs are for seeing.

questions.stem: A goat has four legs. What part are these legs?
hints: They are not the main body.
questions.explanation: Legs are limbs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think legs are the trunk.

questions.stem: What is the main function of an animal's head?
options: To help the animal sense its surroundings and eat
questions.explanation: The head contains the sense organs (eyes, ears, nose) and the mouth, helping the animal sense the world and eat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the head is only for eating.

questions.stem: Does a bird have limbs?
options: No, it only has a head and trunk
Yes, its wings and legs are limbs
No, birds do not have limbs
Yes, only its beak is a limb
hints: What does a bird use to fly?
What does it use to stand?
questions.explanation: A bird's wings and legs are its limbs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think limbs are only arms and legs in humans.

questions.stem: Which part of a dog is its trunk?
hints: The head and legs are attached to it.
questions.explanation: The trunk is the main body of the dog.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the trunk is the dog's nose or tail.

questions.stem: Why do different animals have different types of limbs?
options: To help them move in their own habitat
questions.explanation: Different animals have different limbs to help them move in their specific habitats (water, air, land).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think limbs are just for decoration.

questions.stem: Name the three basic parts of an animal.
questions.explanation: The three main parts are the head, limbs, and trunk.
questions.misconception: Pupils may include the tail, which is an extension of the trunk but not one of the three main parts.

questions.stem: What do we call the middle part of an animal where the head and legs are attached?
hints: It is not the head or limbs.
questions.explanation: The trunk is the main body part.

questions.stem: Ama is looking at a picture of a fish. What are the fish's limbs?
questions.explanation: A fish's fins are its limbs, used for swimming.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think only legs and arms are limbs.

questions.stem: Kwame says 'An elephant's trunk is the same as an animal's trunk.' Is he correct?
options: Yes, they are the same thing
No, an elephant's trunk is its nose, but an animal's trunk is its main body
No, an elephant does not have a trunk
hints: What does an elephant use its trunk for?
questions.explanation: An elephant's trunk is a long nose, but in science, an animal's trunk refers to its main body.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the everyday term with the scientific term.

questions.stem: Which of these animals does NOT have limbs?
hints: Which animal slides on the ground?
questions.explanation: A snake does not have limbs; it moves by slithering.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all animals have legs.

questions.stem: Draw an animal of your choice. Label the head, trunk, and limbs.
hints: Draw a dog or a goat.
Point to the main body, the head, and the legs.
questions.explanation: This tests the ability to identify and label animal parts.

questions.stem: Explain how a dog's limbs and head work together to help it eat.

criteria.description: States the head is used to find or eat food
States the limbs are used to move the dog to the food

hints: How does the dog find food?
How does it get to the food?
questions.explanation: The dog uses its head (nose/eyes) to find food, and its limbs to move towards the food.

questions.stem: Draw a bird and label its limbs.

criteria.description: Labels the wings or legs as limbs

questions.explanation: This tests the understanding that wings are limbs.

questions.stem: Why is it important for animals to have a head, trunk, and limbs?
options: So they can survive, move, and sense their environment
hints: Think about what each part does.
The head senses, limbs move, trunk holds.
questions.explanation: These parts work together to help the animal survive, move, and interact with its environment.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think these parts are just for appearance.

questions.stem: Point to your own head, trunk, and limbs and tell your teacher what each part does.

criteria.description: Points to head and says it is for seeing/hearing/eating
Points to trunk (chest/stomach) and says it is the main body
Points to limbs (arms/legs) and says they are for moving

hints: Your arms and legs are limbs.
questions.explanation: This tests the practical understanding of the three parts.
